Sony Headphones Compared

WH-1000XM3, XM4, XM5, XM6, CH720N and CH520

Research-based

By Lizzy · Updated October 10, 2026

Choosing a Sony headphone is about more than choosing the newest model. The CH520 is a light on-ear headphone without ANC; the CH720N offers lightweight over-ear noise cancellation; the XM range brings different generations of premium features.

This guide is based on published specifications and research, rather than personal testing of every model. Fit, hearing preferences and the seal around glasses can change your experience.

Wearing Comfort

The lightest model is not necessarily the most comfortable. CH520 pads sit on your ears, while the other models surround them. Headband pressure, pad depth and your glasses deserve a trial fit.

ModelWeight / fitWhat to checkScore / 10
XM3255 g · Over-earTraditional over-ear fit. Check ageing pads and whether your ears touch the lining.8.0
XM4254 g · Over-earTraditional padded design. Check ear-cup depth and pressure around glasses.8.5
XM5250 g · Over-earSlim headband and roomy pads. Check for concentrated pressure at the top of your head.7.5
XM6254 g · Over-earWider headband and revised cushioning. Fit improvements remain dependent on your head shape.8.5
CH720N192 g · Over-earLightweight over-ear option. Check the seal and stability when moving.9.0
CH520147 g · On-earLightest here, but on-ear pads press directly on the ears. Check glasses and prolonged pressure.6.5

If you prefer a light over-ear design, start by trying CH720N. For longer sessions, compare headband pressure on XM4, XM5 and XM6 rather than relying on a score alone.

Sound & Noise Cancellation

This editorial dimension gives equal consideration to sound and isolation. If ANC is essential, check the feature itself: an adjustable score does not impose a must-have filter.

ModelSound & isolationANCScore / 10
XM3Bass-forward tuning with active noise cancellation. Age alone does not determine your preferred sound.Yes7.0
XM4Warm, bass-forward sound and premium ANC; not intended as a neutral default tuning.Yes8.0
XM5Full, warm presentation with strong ANC. The tuning may not suit every listener.Yes8.5
XM6Warm presentation; same-method isolation comparisons favour it over XM5, though everyday gains vary.Yes9.0
CH720NEveryday listening with ANC and app EQ. No LDAC; codec support alone does not decide sound quality.Yes6.5
CH520No active noise cancellation and limited passive isolation. Better suited to quiet surroundings.No4.0

The XM6/XM5 isolation observation refers to a same-method RTINGS comparison. Results from different publications are not combined into a single laboratory scale here.

Ecosystem & Design

Connection features, controls and portability matter alongside appearance. These design scores are editorial preferences; your taste may differ.

ModelConnections & portabilityBluetooth codecsScore / 10
XM3Foldable design; lacks the later models’ two-device multipoint.SBC, AAC, aptX, aptX HD, LDAC6.0
XM4Foldable; multipoint disables LDAC on this model.SBC, AAC, LDAC7.5
XM5Minimal styling, non-folding frame; updated firmware supports LDAC with multipoint.SBC, AAC, LDAC8.0
XM6Folding frame and magnetic case; multipoint, LDAC and LC3 require compatible devices.SBC, AAC, LDAC, LC39.0
CH720NPractical plastic build, physical controls and multipoint; does not fold inward.SBC, AAC7.0
CH520Compact on-ear design, multipoint and physical controls; no wired listening or supplied case.SBC, AAC6.0

iPhone’s native Bluetooth does not support LDAC. Android users should also check their device’s codec support. Multipoint usually switches between sources rather than mixing their audio.

Battery life with ANC on / off: XM3: 30 / 38 h; XM4: 30 / 38 h; XM5: 30 / 40 h; XM6: 30 / 40 h; CH720N: 35 / 50 h; CH520: — / 50 h. These are published maximums under specified conditions, not a promise of everyday runtime. All charge by USB-C; CH520 does not provide wired listening.

How the scores work

Scores reflect Lizzy Finds’ editorial assessment of published specifications and research. They are not laboratory measurements or hands-on test results.

Comfort considers fit and pressure; sound and ANC share a dimension equally; ecosystem and design considers connection features, controls and portability. Default priorities are equal.

Overall score = 10 × sum of (dimension score × priority) ÷ sum of priorities.

Price score = 1 + 9 × (highest price − model price) ÷ (highest price − lowest price). Equal prices all receive 10. The active comparison set defines this range.

Ranking uses unrounded scores. Models within 0.05 points of the top score are shown as tied. Displayed scores have one decimal place. With price priority set to zero, all six models can participate without a quote.

This tool does not impose an absolute budget limit or an ANC requirement. Check those separately before buying, and inspect the battery, pads and warranty of older stock.
